newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to offer two drug-makers before year-end.
newsitem.headline: Poland to offer two drug-makers before year-end.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry, the former privatisation ministry, will invite investor bids for stakes in two pharmaceutical companies before the end of the year, an official involved in the privatisation process said.

PAP news agency quoted Miroslaw Dlugosz, the president of the Polish Institute of Management advising the ministry on the sale of the pharmaceutical sector, as saying three other larger drug-makers would be offered to investors later.
"By the end of December the treasury ministry will invite investors to a tender for shares in Polfa Rzeszow SA and Polfa Krakow SA," Dlugosz was quoted as saying.
The three larger companies slated for sale are Polfa Tarchomin, Polfa Poznan and Polfa Starogard Szczecinski.
Out of Poland's 15 pharmaceutical firms formerly belonging to the Polfa group, Jelfa and Polfa Kutno have been privatised.
